summary: Elevated 5xx in prod (eu-west) after balancer hotpath routed high fanout to small runtime set causing OOM-crashwave
description:
Issue summary: Beginning ~2026-03-13 18:20 UTC we observed a sharp rise in 502/503/504 responses from api-gateway in eu-west. Error rate peaked ~18:35 UTC and remains elevated for some customer tenants. Impact: Multiple dedicated customers (including BrightHome AI) saw failed inference requests and streaming disconnects; latency for surviving requests increased 3-4x. Scope: localized to eu-west prod cluster and correlated with balancer scale events and a large embedding + chat mix from a single tenant.

Environment: prod (eu-west), dedicated capacity pool for BrightHome AI.

Steps to reproduce (approx): 1) High fanout embedding upload and chat traffic from tenant during scheduled marketing burst. 2) Ingress balancer entered 'hotpath' routing because of sudden conn concentration. 3) Balancer favored a small subset of runtimes (hotset) and kept routing new sessions there. 4) Runtimes in hotset showed growing memory fragmentation and GPU OOM restarts. 5) api-gateway returned 502/503 while retry amplification increased load.

Observed behavior & metrics: - api-gateway 5xx spike: baseline <0.2% -> 12% at peak. - Runtime restarts: nvml OOMs (driver logs) increased from 0 to ~20 events/min. - Balancer metrics: hotset size shrank from ~8 to 2 nodes during surge; per-node in-flight connections grew to ~600. - Autoscaler showed delayed reaction due to cooldown policy. - Token-level traces show repeated hedged retries from client SDK triggering additional fanout.

Initial hypothesis: balancer routing decision combined with priority/token distribution and hedged retries created a positive feedback loop that focused load on a small runtime subset, causing memory fragmentation and GPU OOMs. Autoscaler cooldown and prewarm logic prevented immediate absorption of load.

Relevant logs/observables (snips): 
- runtime stderr: "[nvml] GPU 0: out of memory allocating kv cache slot"
- runtime watchdog: "SIGABRT: exit 137 - oom_kill"
- balancer log: "route_selection: hotpath chosen, preferred_pool=hotset-7, target_nodes=2"
- api-gateway: "upstream response 502 from 10.3.42.11: upstream closed connection"

Customer impact notes: BrightHome AI large-batch embed & chat workflows failed intermittently; customers reported timeouts in production flows.

Attach: dashboards: apigw/5xx-eu-west, runtime/gpu-ooms-eu-west, balancer/hotpath-heatmap.
comments: 2026-03-13 18:45 - Support (Aisha): Alert triaged. Notified SRE on-call and BrightHome AI CSM. Collecting traces and dashboards.
2026-03-13 18:52 - SRE (Marco): Confirmed runtime OOMs and balancer hotset contraction. Spun up temporary extra workers in eu-west to relieve hotset.
2026-03-13 19:05 - Support (Aisha): Customer BrightHome AI reports partial recovery but intermittent failures persist for long streaming sessions.
2026-03-13 19:22 - SRE (Marco): Applied balancer patch to cap per-node in-flight connections and adjusted autoscaler cooldown for emergency scaling. Observing metrics.
2026-03-14 08:10 - CSM (Lina Moreno): Customer requests root cause and timeline for incident impact. Requested postmortem and follow-up mitigation plan.
2026-03-14 12:03 - SRE (Marco): Added linked GH PR with fixes for balancer heuristics and an immediate hotfix to prevent preference collapse. See PR linked in ticket.
investigation_notes: Checked balancer telemetry: hotpath selection algorithm moved to a narrow hotset when connection distribution skew exceeded threshold. The threshold was too aggressive for mixed embed+chat workloads.

Examined runtime memory metrics: fragmentation pattern consistent with many short-lived KV cache allocations and large embedding tensors; repeated allocations caused CUDA OOMs followed by watchdog restarts.
Autoscaler analysis: emergency scale triggers were delayed because prewarm policy required 90s stabilization; during spike this prevented new capacity from joining hotset quickly.
Correlation: tenant SDK hedged-retry behavior amplified the hotset concentration; SDK retries were set to aggressive defaults in this tenant's integration.
Related historical issues: balancer hotset contraction surfaced in SUP-305678 under different load shapes; linked for context.
resolution_notes: Mitigations applied (short-term): 1) emergency scale + added 6 warm runtimes to eu-west pool; 2) patched balancer to enforce per-node in-flight connection cap and avoid collapsing hotset below 4 nodes; 3) temporarily increased autoscaler aggressiveness for the affected pool; 4) recommended tenant change: reduce hedged-retry aggressiveness and stagger embedding uploads.

Longer-term actions: 1) merge PR runtime/pull/9852 to add fragmentation-aware scheduling; 2) update balancer heuristics to consider recent restart counts and memory fragmentation signals; 3) publish runbook entry for hotpath incidents and add automated mitigation to reduce mean time to remediate; 4) follow up with BrightHome AI on SDK retry tuning and provide quota guidance.
Current status: error rate reduced to ~0.8% by 2026-03-14 11:00 UTC. Monitoring for reoccurrence. Postmortem scheduled with SRE/Eng/CSM on 2026-03-16.
Owner for follow-up tasks: Marco Ruiz (SRE) for balancer patch rollout; Lina Moreno (CSM) to coordinate customer follow-up; Product to prioritize fragmentation scheduling in next cycle.
